Container.Name: tape
Container.Overview: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier for CEF Tracker + Keystone. ONE neutral template for dev and prod: at creation set Name (tape / tape-dev), image tag (:stable for prod, :dev for dev), network + a static IP if you use one, and the discrete DB_* vars pointing at the tape-db container. The app assembles the DB connection string from DB_HOST/DB_PORT/DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD/DB_NAME (§2 B.10), or set DATABASE_URL to override with a full connection string. Everything else, including the Schwab/FRED/Tiingo credentials, is database-managed via the admin API, seeded with shipped defaults — see the header comment.
Container.Description: Tape — Schwab-backed market + account data tier (one neutral template, dev+prod).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Encrypted token store. REQUIRED - set an absolute path on a POOL (e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/tape/data, or .../tape-dev/data for a dev container). Do NOT leave it blank and do not point it at the RAM-backed root filesystem. The retrievable ops/error logs also default to a subdirectory of this mount.

Config.Name: Backups
Config.Description: Where the scheduled pg_dump lands. REQUIRED for a real backup: WITHOUT this mount the dump is written INSIDE the container and destroyed by the next update — the job still reports success, which is why it went unnoticed for months. Set an absolute path on a POOL DIFFERENT from the one holding the DB container's data (e.g. /mnt/<other-pool>/appdata/tape/backups), so one pool failure cannot take both the warehouse and its only backup. The app WARNS (ntfy) at boot and at every dump if this path is not a persistent mount. ⚠️ THIS MOUNT IS THE BACKUP_DIR SETTING — there is deliberately no BACKUP_DIR Variable, because the two must never disagree: a Variable pointing anywhere other than this mount point would send dumps into the container filesystem, which is the exact silent failure above.

Config.Name: Shared alerting config
Config.Description: READ-ONLY mount of the shared fleet config directory — set the host path to the directory holding configs/alerting.env (EMAIL_TO, EMAIL_FROM, SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, and the ntfy topics NTFY_URL_TAPE / NTFY_URL_DEV / NTFY_URL_PROD). THIS MOUNT IS BOTH ALERT CHANNELS, ntfy AND email: both are deliberately read from that file at send time and NEVER from a per-container environment variable, because an environment variable is visible to anyone who can run a container inspect and both an SMTP password and an ntfy topic are real credentials. The container path is FIXED at /kw_shared (T-CRED-PURGE-1 — the app hardcodes it, there is no SHARED_ROOT Variable to keep in sync any more). Without this mount both channels are unreachable and every alert this service raises goes NOWHERE (it says so loudly in the boot log). One file serves the whole fleet, so rotating the password, moving the inbox or repointing a topic is one edit rather than one per container.

Config.Name: TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY
Config.Description: Fernet key for token-at-rest encryption AND for every encrypted app_config credential row (Schwab app key/secret, FRED/Tiingo API keys, the legacy shared API key — set those via the admin API once this container is up). REQUIRED - the key that decrypts the store cannot itself live inside it.

Config.Name: DB_HOST
Config.Description: Warehouse DB host - the address of the tape-db container serving THIS environment

Config.Name: DB_USER
Config.Description: Warehouse DB user (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_USER)

Config.Name: DB_PASSWORD
Config.Description: Warehouse DB password (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_PASSWORD)

Config.Name: DB_NAME
Config.Description: Warehouse DB name (matches the tape-db container's POSTGRES_DB)

Config.Name: DATABASE_URL
Config.Description: OPTIONAL override — full SQLAlchemy URL (postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/db). Leave BLANK to use the discrete DB_* vars above; if set, it wins.

Config.Name: DEPLOY_ENV
Config.Description: REQUIRED - type prod or dev. It selects which shared ntfy topic this container falls back to when NTFY_URL_TAPE is not set (NTFY_URL_PROD or NTFY_URL_DEV) and which keys the shared file must carry. DELIBERATELY BLANK: a default here would silently put a dev deployment on the prod topic, and the symptom of that is an incident that paged the wrong place. Case does not matter.
